headline: Critical Vulnerabilities Patched: SonicWall, VMware, Metabase, and Cisco Flaws Addressed
summary:
This daily summary highlights critical security updates and new vulnerabilities impacting various software and hardware.  SonicWall zero-days (CVE-2026-15409, CVE-2026-15410) are now being actively exploited for ransomware deployment, escalating their threat level. VMware has patched a critical VM escape flaw (CVE-2026-47876) in ESXi, with active exploitation confirmed for CVE-2026-59310, allowing persistent reverse SSH tunnels. The Metabase zero-day SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-72898) continues widespread exploitation, with LexisNexis confirming an incident. Microsoft's August Patch Tuesday addresses over 400 vulnerabilities, including a Windows privilege escalation zero-day (CVE-2026-68820) exploited by the Lazarus Group.

CISA warns of Gunra ransomware targeting critical infrastructure, utilizing vulnerabilities in Fortinet and Schneider Electric devices, with new TTPs including session hijacking and MFA bypass. A LiteLLM AI supply chain attack by Team PCP exposed over 2,500 companies through a novel secondary exfiltration technique using GitHub repositories. New threats include 'Ghostjacking' and 'GhostSplice' attacks targeting AI agents, and AI-powered cyberattacks impacting major U.S. corporations. Cisco has patched a zero-day DoS vulnerability in its Secure Firewall (CVE-2026-20349). Zoom has addressed a zero-click RCE flaw in its conferencing app, and Ivanti has released patches for critical RCE vulnerabilities in its Endpoint Manager.

Organizations are strongly advised to apply all available patches and review security configurations to mitigate these evolving threats.

articles.headline: SonicWall Zero-Days Exploited for Weeks Before Public Disclosure
articles.title: SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days Exploited in Wild
articles.excerpt: Two critical zero-day vulnerabilities in SonicWall's SMA 1000 series appliances, CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410, were actively exploited by threat actors for at least three weeks before being disclosed and patched. According to Volexity, attackers chained the flaws—an SSRF and a code injection—to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution with root privileges. The attackers focused on stealth and persistence, deploying custom malware named ROOTRUN and KNUCKLEBALL to maintain long-term access for credential theft and network monitoring. CISA has added both vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog, mandating urgent patching for federal agencies.
articles.updateSummary: CISA confirms SonicWall SMA zero-days (CVE-2026-15409, CVE-2026-15410) are now actively exploited by ransomware groups for initial network access, urging immediate patching.
articles.updateContent: New intelligence indicates that the critical SonicWall SMA 1000 series zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410, are now being actively leveraged by ransomware groups. Previously, exploitation focused on stealthy persistence and credential theft for potential espionage. However, CISA's latest update highlights that these flaws are now a primary vector for initial access, allowing ransomware operators to bypass perimeter defenses and deploy their payloads. This escalation significantly increases the immediate threat level, making urgent patching and post-compromise hunting critical for all organizations using affected devices. The shift to ransomware groups underscores a more destructive and widespread impact than initially reported.

articles.headline: VMware Patches Critical VM Escape Flaw (CVE-2026-47876) in ESXi
articles.title: VMware Patches Critical ESXi VM Escape Vulnerability
articles.excerpt: Broadcom has issued security updates for multiple VMware products, addressing five vulnerabilities, including a critical VM escape flaw in ESXi (CVE-2026-47876). This vulnerability allows an attacker with administrative privileges on a guest VM to execute code on the underlying host. Two additional critical flaws (CVE-2026-59309, CVE-2026-59310) in vCenter permit unauthenticated access and remote code execution. Organizations are urged to apply the patches immediately to prevent potential hypervisor compromise and full environment takeover.
articles.updateSummary: Threat actors are now mass-scanning for VMware vCenter flaws (CVE-2026-59309), and CVE-2026-59310 is under active exploitation to deploy backdoors.
articles.updateContent: Following the initial advisory, security researchers have observed widespread scanning activity targeting VMware vCenter Server instances for CVE-2026-59309, indicating imminent mass exploitation. More critically, CVE-2026-59310 is now confirmed to be actively exploited in the wild. Attackers are leveraging this flaw to write malicious cron jobs that establish persistent reverse SSH tunnels using the `reverse_ssh` tool, compromising over 360 unique IP addresses globally. Organizations must prioritize patching and hunt for compromise using the newly identified IOCs, including `reverse_ssh` file presence and outbound SSH traffic from vCenter.

articles.headline: Metabase Zero-Day SQLi Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Actively Exploited
articles.title: Metabase Zero-Day Flaw Exploited to Steal Data
articles.excerpt: A critical, unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the Metabase analytics platform, rated CVSS 10.0, is being actively exploited in the wild. Tracked as GHSA-vwf4-m7j8-wcjf, the flaw allows attackers to gain full administrator access. The exploit has already led to data breaches at companies like Framework and Tally, where attackers exfiltrated sensitive customer information. Metabase has released patches and urges all users of self-hosted instances to update immediately.
articles.updateSummary: CVE-2026-72898 assigned to Metabase SQLi flaw; LexisNexis confirmed as new victim, and a Sigma rule for detection is now available.
articles.updateContent: The critical Metabase SQL injection vulnerability, previously tracked as GHSA-vwf4-m7j8-wcjf, has now been officially assigned CVE-2026-72898, enhancing its visibility and tracking. Exploitation continues to be widespread, with LexisNexis publicly confirming an incident related to the flaw, adding to previously reported victims like Framework and Tally. For improved detection, a detailed Sigma rule has been provided to help organizations identify exploitation attempts by monitoring specific log patterns for POST requests to /api/session/reset_password followed by GET requests to /api/user/current.

articles.headline: Lazarus Group Exploits Windows Zero-Day in Espionage Campaign
articles.title: Lazarus Group Uses Windows Zero-Day CVE-2026-68820 for SYSTEM-Level Access
articles.excerpt: The North Korean state-sponsored Lazarus Group is actively exploiting a zero-day privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-68820) in a core Windows driver. The flaw, patched in Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday, is being used in the 'Operation Dream Job' campaign to deploy a rootkit and target defense and aerospace organizations. Attackers gain SYSTEM privileges to disable security software and conduct espionage.
articles.updateSummary: Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday addresses over 400 vulnerabilities, including 42 critical flaws and the actively exploited zero-day CVE-2026-68820, urging immediate patching.
articles.updateContent: Microsoft has released its August 2026 Patch Tuesday, fixing over 400 vulnerabilities across its products, with 42 rated critical. This comprehensive update includes the patch for CVE-2026-68820, the Windows privilege escalation zero-day actively exploited by the Lazarus Group. Other notable fixes include CVE-2026-62832 (Windows User Profile Service privilege escalation) and CVE-2026-62878 (potentially wormable RCE in Windows DNS Server). Organizations are strongly advised to apply these updates immediately to mitigate widespread risks.

articles.headline: CISA Warns of Gunra RaaS Targeting Critical Infrastructure
articles.title: CISA Issues Alert on Gunra Ransomware Targeting Global Sectors
articles.excerpt: A joint advisory from CISA, FBI, NSA, and South Korean authorities warns of the Gunra Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS). Derived from leaked Conti source code, the group uses double extortion tactics, targeting critical infrastructure sectors like healthcare and government worldwide. The advisory details TTPs, including exploitation of known vulnerabilities and default credentials, and provides mitigation guidance.
articles.updateSummary: New advisory details Gunra ransomware's exploitation of Fortinet and Schneider Electric flaws, including MFA bypass and session hijacking, demanding multi-million dollar ransoms.
articles.updateContent: The updated advisory from CISA, FBI, NSA, DC3, USSS, and KNPA provides critical new details on Gunra ransomware. It specifically identifies vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiOS/FortiProxy and Schneider Electric PowerLogic (CVE-2024-5559) as initial access vectors. New TTPs include session hijacking via SSL-VPN manipulation, MFA bypass through VDI portal tampering, and lateral movement using PsExec/WMIC. The group also employs defense evasion by deleting logs and demands multi-million dollar ransoms. New hunting hints include specific URL patterns, process names, and log analysis for these advanced tactics.

articles.headline: LiteLLM AI Supply Chain Attack Exposes 2,500+ Companies
articles.title: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack Harvests Credentials from 2,500 Firms
articles.excerpt: A major supply chain attack targeting the open-source AI framework LiteLLM has exposed over 2,500 companies and 434,000 CI/CD pipelines. The threat actor, Team PCP, published malicious versions of the popular Python package on PyPI to harvest cloud credentials, API keys, and other secrets from AI development environments. The incident is considered the largest AI infrastructure breach of 2026.
articles.updateSummary: New details reveal sophisticated secondary exfiltration method using victim's GitHub to create public repositories for stolen credentials.
articles.updateContent: The attack, attributed to Team PCP, utilized a sophisticated secondary exfiltration technique. If direct outbound connections were blocked, the malware would leverage the victim's own GitHub credentials to create a new public repository. Stolen secrets were then uploaded as release assets to this repository, making the exfiltrated data appear as legitimate activity and publicly exposing sensitive information. This method highlights the advanced nature of the threat and the critical need for auditing source control activity.

articles.headline: Ghostjacking & GhostSplice Attacks Target AI Agents
articles.title: New Attacks Ghostjack and GhostSplice Target AI Agents
articles.excerpt: Security researchers have unveiled 'Ghostjacking' and 'GhostSplice,' two novel attack techniques that manipulate AI coding assistants. Ghostjacking uses poisoned logs for indirect prompt injection, while GhostSplice splits malicious commands across trusted channels. These attacks highlight emerging risks in enterprise AI deployments, showing how agents can be tricked into exfiltrating data or executing malicious commands.

articles.headline: AI-Powered Cyberattacks Hit Major US Corporations in 2026
articles.title: AI-Driven Cyberattacks Target Major US Companies
articles.excerpt: Throughout 2026, a surge of AI-enhanced cyberattacks has impacted major U.S. corporations across nearly every sector, including Nike, Wynn Resorts, Coca-Cola, and Stryker. Attackers are using AI to improve social engineering and ransomware campaigns, leading to widespread data breaches, operational shutdowns, and significant financial demands.

articles.headline: Cisco Patches Firewall Zero-Day Exploited for DoS Attacks
articles.title: Cisco Patches Exploited Firewall Zero-Day (CVE-2026-20349)
articles.excerpt: Cisco has patched a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-20349) in its Secure Firewall ASA and FTD devices that is being actively exploited. The flaw allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) condition, disrupting network traffic. Customers are urged to apply the updates immediately.

articles.headline: Zoom Patches Zero-Click RCE Flaw in Conferencing App
articles.title: Zoom Patches Critical Zero-Click Remote Code Execution Flaw
articles.excerpt: Zoom has patched a critical zero-click remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in its video conferencing client. The flaw, located in the annotation feature, could have allowed a meeting participant to execute arbitrary code on another participant's machine without any user interaction. All users are urged to update their Zoom clients immediately.

articles.headline: Ivanti Patches Critical RCE Flaws in Endpoint Manager
articles.title: Ivanti Patches Critical RCE Vulnerabilities in EPM
articles.excerpt: Ivanti has released patches for several critical, remotely exploitable vulnerabilities in its Endpoint Manager (EPM) solution. These flaws could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable systems, potentially leading to a full compromise of managed endpoints. Given Ivanti's history as a target, immediate patching is advised.
